stories.title: Design in code, not in pictures of it: the prototype becomes the source, the file a mirror
stories.blurb: Jon Sabutis reviews code prototypes and regenerates the design file from them after each pass, because a file shows one state at one width while the product is every other state. Worth reading for the closing list of what designers should learn instead of syntax: layout flow, empty and failed states, data shape, what a screen reader announces, and testing at 320 pixels with the longest real name.

stories.title: A US lawsuit over an AI-generated meme character tests how many prompts make a work protectable
stories.blurb: Do Big Studios is suing in a California federal court after receiving a cease and desist over Tung Tung Tung Sahur, a character its teenage creator generated with seven prompts in about fifteen minutes. The piece spells out the client stakes either way: if prompts are not enough, AI-assisted logos and characters may be free to copy; if they are, clients may ask why they pay for handmade work.
